result: The authors determined the first 3D EM structure of the human PRC2-AEBP2 complex at 21 Å resolution. The complex has a molecular mass of ~275 kDa with an elongated shape (16 nm × 7 nm) consisting of four lobes (A, B, C, D) interconnected by two arms. Mild glutaraldehyde cross-linking (0.015%) improved complex stability for structural analysis.
status_reasoning: Claims C4, C17-C21 provide converging evidence from size-exclusion chromatography, negative-stain EM, and 3D reconstruction with appropriate resolution estimation using Fourier shell correlation. The structural characterization is well-documented with multiple complementary measurements and appropriate controls (cross-linked vs non-cross-linked samples).

result: Using a novel internal GFP tagging method combined with EM, the authors localized all PRC2 subunits and their functional domains within the structure. EED WD40 is at Lobe A, RbAp48 WD40 at Lobe D, Ezh2 SANT domains between Lobes A-B, Ezh2 SET domain at Lobe B, Suz12 N-terminus at Lobe C terminating at Lobe B, and AEBP2 running from Lobe A/Arm 1 to Arm 2/Lobe D. The complex contains a single copy of each subunit.
status_reasoning: Claims C5, C37-C50 describe a systematic localization strategy using multiple tagged constructs with redundant labeling positions. The observation of single tag densities per construct (C49) supports stoichiometry claims. The localizations are internally consistent with cross-linking data (C42) and integrate well with known crystal structures, providing strong converging evidence for the architectural model.

result: Chemical cross-linking with isotope-labeled DSSG combined with mass spectrometry identified extensive inter- and intra-molecular interactions within PRC2-AEBP2. Key findings include: EED WD40 interacts with Ezh2 N-terminus; Ezh2 SANT domains interact with each other and with AEBP2/Suz12; the SET domain of Ezh2 and Zn fingers of Suz12 and AEBP2 form a trimeric subcomplex; RbAp48, central Suz12, and AEBP2 undergo extensive interactions. AEBP2 plays a major coordinating role, explaining its stabilizing effect.
status_reasoning: Claims C22-C36 describe cross-linking data validated against known crystal structures (C22, C31) and consistent with EM localization data. The use of isotope-labeled cross-linkers with appropriate mass spectrometry identification provides rigorous evidence. The cross-linking distances are appropriate for the DSSG linker length, and the data converge with structural localization to support the interaction map and AEBP2's coordinating role.

result: Integration of the EM structure with existing crystal structures reveals the spatial organization of functional domains. The Ezh2 SET domain forms a structural core with EED WD40 and Suz12 VEFS domains. The two SANT domains of Ezh2 are positioned between EED WD40 and the SET domain. The two WD40 domains (EED and RbAp48) are ~100 Å apart at opposite ends of the structure, consistent with the length of a histone H3 tail.
status_reasoning: Claims C30, C38, C57-C58, C60, C62, C69-C71 integrate crystallographic data with the EM structure through rigid-body docking validated by tag localization. The ~100 Å distance measurement between WD40 domains (C70) is directly observable from the structure and the comparison to histone H3 tail length (C71) is based on established structural knowledge, providing a reasonable structural interpretation.

result: The authors propose mechanistic models for PRC2 regulation based on their structure. They suggest that SANT domains may transmit H3K27me3 binding signals from EED to the SET domain, and that the proximity of Suz12 VEFS and Ezh2 SET domains explains how H3K4me3/H3K36me2-3 inhibition could be transferred to regulate methyltransferase activity. These models integrate prior biochemical findings with the new structural context.

The work generates testable hypotheses for future research.
